# Lesson diagrams: what to use

85 diagrams that lessons and exams ask for are drawn by a template or a symbol that exists. Find yours by name here, then `npm run render -- --template <id> --explain` (a template) or write a recipe with the symbol. The "how" says what to set. The diagram inventory (`docs/diagram-inventory.md`) lists every diagram type, including those that are not drawn yet (168 need new symbols, templates or flow diagrams; 40 are graphs, tables and spectra, which PracDraw does not draw).

## Chemistry, KS4

| diagram | courses | use | how |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Particle diagram of an element, a compound or a mixture | 8464, 8462 | symbol `particleBox` | Use the particleBox symbol: set `substance` (element, molecules, compound, mixtureElements, mixtureCompounds or mixtureElementCompound), `state` (gas, liquid or solid), `count` (6 to 40; a molecule counts as one) and, for a compound, `formula` (AB, AB2 or A2B). The kinds of particle differ by size and by fill (white, grey tint with hatch, solid black); `motion` adds arrows. The symbol has no text: label it with label items. |
| Periodic table (outline with groups, periods and metal divider) | 8464, 8462 | symbol `periodicTable` | Use the periodicTable symbol: the first 20 or the first 36 elements in 18 columns and 4 rows of square cells (the d block is ten cells, scandium to zinc). `content` is the symbol, the atomic number, both, the relative atomic mass, or blank; `groups` numbers the groups 1 to 7 and 0 (KS4), 1 to 18 (IUPAC) or not at all; one highlight (an element, a group or a period, in that order of precedence) is a heavy ring on the cell edges; `divider` draws the stepped line between metals and non-metals; `shading` shades metals or blocks with a tint and, in photocopy-safe mode, a hatch. |
| A Group 1 metal reacting with water | 8464, 8462 | template `groupOneWater` | Use the groupOneWater template: a beaker of water with a piece of lithium floating at the surface, bubbles below it and a burning splint above. |
| Halogen displacement reactions in test tubes | 8464, 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with three or four tubes in a rack. Tubes hold potassium chloride, bromide or iodide solution (Colourless solution preset) and, after adding a halogen water, the Orange preset (bromine) or the Brown preset (iodine). Label each tube with the pair of chemicals. A tube where nothing happens keeps its first colour. |
| Particle diagrams of a solid, a liquid and a gas | 8464, 8462 | symbol `particleBox` | Use three particleBox parts side by side with `state` solid, liquid and gas (same substance and count, `motion` on if wanted), and label them with label items. A solid is a lattice in contact on the floor of the box, a liquid an irregular touching heap in the lower part, a gas particles spread through the box. |
| Dot-and-cross diagram of an ionic compound | 8464, 8462 | symbol `ionicDotCross` | Use the ionicDotCross symbol: choose the metal (Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, Al), the non-metal (N, O, F, S, Cl, Br), the `stage` (transfer: the atoms with curved arrows for the electrons that move; ions: each ion in square brackets with its charge at the top right), `inner` shells on or off and the `marks`. The number of ions follows from the charges (MgCl2 shows three ions, Al2O3 five), so the ratio can be counted. The metal ion shows no outer electrons and the non-metal ion a full outer shell. |
| Dot-and-cross diagram of a simple covalent molecule | 8464, 8462 | symbol `covalentDotCross` | Use the covalentDotCross symbol: choose one of 13 small molecules (H2, Cl2, O2, N2, HCl, H2O, NH3, CH4, CO2, HF, F2, C2H4, C2H6), the `layout` (overlapping circles, or circles apart with the shared pairs between them) and the `marks` (dots and crosses, swapped, or dots and open rings). One circle for the outer shell of each atom; each shared pair is one cross and one dot (two and three pairs for a double and a triple bond); the other outer electrons stay on the atom's own circle, with lone pairs drawn as pairs; inner shells are not drawn. The element symbol is written in each circle. |
| Sodium chloride lattice in three dimensions (ball and stick) | 8464, 8462, 7405 | symbol `ionicLattice3D` | Use the ionicLattice3D symbol: a 3 by 3 by 3 block of 27 ions in the oblique view, 14 Cl- (large, grey with hatch) and 13 Na+ (small, white), with 54 bonds between unlike ions and the three hidden back bonds dashed. Set `bonds` off to show the ions alone. Add the names or the charges of the ions with label items: the symbol has no text. |
| Diamond (giant covalent, tetrahedral) | 8464, 8462, 7405 | symbol `diamondStructure` | Use the diamondStructure symbol: a cluster of 17 carbon atoms (one atom, its four neighbours and their twelve other neighbours) with 16 bonds, in the oblique view turned about the vertical axis so that no circles overlap. Front bonds are heavy and rear bonds thin. With `stubs` on (the default), a short line at every outer atom shows the bonds that go on, so that each atom shows four. Add "each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds" with a label item: the symbol has no text. |
| Graphite (layers of hexagons) | 8464, 8462, 7405 | symbol `graphiteStructure` | Use the graphiteStructure symbol: 2 to 4 (default 3) identical sheets one above the other, each a patch of two rows of three hexagons (22 atoms) in the oblique view, with a short stub at every edge atom to show that the net goes on. With `forces` on (the default) four dotted vertical lines between each pair of sheets show the weak forces. Add the labels (layer, weak forces) with label items: the symbol has no text. |
| Buckminsterfullerene C60 | 8464, 8462 | symbol `fullereneC60` | Use the fullereneC60 symbol: the truncated icosahedron of 60 carbon atoms and 90 bonds, seen from the direction of a pentagon and tilted a little, as an opaque ball: only the 30 atoms and 40 bonds on faces that face the viewer are drawn. Set `pentagons` on to shade the visible pentagons (grey with hatch). Add the name or "C60" with a label item: the symbol has no text. |
| Mass change in an open and a closed flask on a balance | 8464, 8462 | template `massLoss` | Use the massLoss template: a conical flask on the balance with marble chips, acid and bubbles, a cotton wool plug in the neck, and the balance reading as text. Draw it twice side by side for 'before' and 'after' with readings such as 150.00 g and 149.20 g. For a closed system swap the cotton wool plug for a bung and give both pictures the same reading. |
| Heating magnesium in a crucible with a lid (mass gain) | 8464, 8462 | template `magnesiumInCrucible` | Use the magnesiumInCrucible template: a lidded crucible on a pipeclay triangle on a tripod, the flame touching its base, and magnesium ribbon in the crucible. |
| Thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate with a limewater test | 8464, 8462 | template `thermalDecomposition` | Use the thermalDecomposition template: a boiling tube of green copper carbonate powder held by a clamp, sloping with its mouth a little higher than its closed end, a Bunsen flame under the powder, a one-hole bung with a delivery tube into a test tube of limewater in a rack. Labels: copper carbonate, heat, delivery tube, limewater. The limewater turns cloudy. |
| Reading a burette or measuring cylinder (enlarged scale) | 8464, 8462 | symbol `scaleWindow` | Use the magnified scale: a section of a burette or measuring cylinder with divisions and the end values, a liquid with a meniscus, and the reading set with the Reading field. The student writes the reading to the nearest half division. Blank mode removes the answer. |
| Titration apparatus (burette, flask and white tile) | 8462, 7405 | template `titration` | Use the titration template: a burette clamped upright with its tip inside the neck of a conical flask, the flask on a white tile with alkali and an indicator (Pink preset for phenolphthalein), labels for each part. Add the volumetricPipette and pipetteFiller beside it for the stage where the alkali is measured. |
| Metals in dilute acid in test tubes (rate of bubbling) | 8464, 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with four tubes in a rack, each with a small piece of a different metal (the metal ribbon symbol, labelled) in Colourless solution. Bubbles at three levels, because the contents model has many, few and none and no fourth level: many in magnesium, few in zinc and in iron, none in copper. Labels name the metals and the acid. Optional gas test above one tube. |
| Displacement of a metal from a salt solution | 8464, 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template: tubes with a metal strip or an iron nail in copper sulfate solution (Blue preset) before and after, the blue fading and a brown deposit as a powder layer at the foot of the tube (powder lies at the bottom of a tube; the strip or nail stands in the solution above it); a tube with no change for a less reactive metal. Labels give the metals and the solution. |
| Heating a metal oxide with carbon and testing the gas | 8464, 8462 | template `thermalDecomposition` | Use the thermalDecomposition template with a black mixture of copper oxide and carbon (Black powder preset) in the boiling tube, the delivery tube into limewater in a test tube, and the Bunsen under the powder. Optional labels: 'copper oxide and carbon', 'limewater turns cloudy'. |
| Preparing a pure dry soluble salt (react, filter, evaporate) | 8464, 8462 | template `crystallisation` | Three pictures in order, all existing templates. Step 1, heatingBeaker: warm dilute acid in a beaker on a gauze, with the insoluble oxide or carbonate added in excess and stirred (glass rod). Step 2, filtration: funnel and filter paper over a conical flask, the unreacted solid on the paper. Step 3, crystallisation (the evaporating basin on a beaker of water or on the gauze). Labels name each step. |
| pH scale with universal indicator colours | 8464, 8462 | symbol `phScale` | Use the phScale symbol: a strip of 15 equal cells numbered 0 to 14 in the universal indicator colours (red, orange, yellow, green at 7, blue, purple), with brackets for acidic (below 7), neutral (7) and alkaline (above 7) and, if wanted, four example substances at their pH (lemon juice, water, soap, bleach). In photocopy-safe mode every cell is white with its number and outline. For a vertical strip set orientation to vertical and make the box tall (for example 70 wide and 420 high): the symbol does not swap the box itself. |
| Apparatus for electrolysis of a molten compound | 8464, 8462 | template `electrolysisMolten` | Use the electrolysisMolten template: a crucible on a pipeclay triangle on a tripod, heated by a Bunsen burner; two rods held by one stand with two clamps that each grip a rod; two wires to a power supply that do not cross. The note about the fume cupboard is plain text. |
| Electrolysis of a solution with gas collected in inverted tubes | 8464, 8462 | template `electrolysis` | Use the electrolysis template: the cell with two electrodes, two upside-down test tubes over the electrodes, gas in both tubes with about twice the volume over the negative electrode for a sodium sulfate solution, wires to a power supply. Label the electrodes + and -, and the gases. |
| Electrolysis of an aqueous solution with a Petri dish lid (required practical) | 8464, 8462 | template `electrolysisBeaker` | Use the electrolysisBeaker template: a beaker of solution with a lid on its rim, a carbon rod through each of two holes, a crocodile clip on the top of each rod, wires to a low-voltage supply. A strip of blue litmus paper held at the anode for chlorine. Labels: carbon electrodes, solution, supply. |
| Reaction profile (energy level diagram): exothermic and endothermic | 8464, 8462 | symbol `reactionProfile` | Use the reactionProfile symbol: the axes "Energy" and "Progress of reaction" and a smooth curve from a flat reactants level over a rounded peak to a flat products level (exothermic: the products are lower; endothermic: higher). `activation` draws the double-headed activation energy arrow, `change` the arrow for the overall energy change, `catalyst` a lower dashed route, and `levels` labels the two levels in words, as two worked formula equations, or as blank lines to write on. |
| Temperature change of a reaction in a polystyrene cup (required practical) | 8464, 8462 | template `temperatureChange` | Use the temperatureChange template: a polystyrene cup with a lid in a beaker, a thermometer through the lid hole, the solution at about 50 percent. Label cup, lid, thermometer, beaker. |
| Simple cell: two metals in an electrolyte with a voltmeter | 8462 | template `simpleCell` | Use the simpleCell template: a beaker of electrolyte with a zinc strip and a copper strip 44 u apart, their tips under the surface, and wires with clips to a voltmeter; zinc is marked minus and copper plus. |
| Rate of reaction: gas collected in a gas syringe | 8464, 8462 | template `rateGasSyringe` | Use the rateGasSyringe template: a conical flask of acid with marble chips and bubbles, a bung and a tube to a gas syringe held by a clamp, a stopwatch beside the stand. Label flask, acid, marble chips, gas syringe, stopwatch. |
| Rate of reaction: gas collected over water | 8464, 8462 | template `rateGasOverWater` | Use the rateGasOverWater template: a flask of acid with magnesium ribbon, a one-hole bung and delivery tube to a trough of water, an upside-down measuring cylinder full of water held by a clamp over the tube end, a stopwatch. Label flask, bung, delivery tube, trough, measuring cylinder. |
| Rate of reaction measured by loss of mass | 8464, 8462 | template `massLoss` | Use the massLoss template: a conical flask of acid with marble chips on a balance, a cotton wool plug in the neck so that spray stays in and the gas escapes, and a stopwatch beside the balance. Lumps, liquid and bubbles in the flask. |
| Rate of reaction: disappearing cross (sodium thiosulfate and acid) | 8464, 8462 | template `disappearingCross` | Use the disappearingCross template: a flask on a paper with a cross, the observer looking down into the flask, a stopwatch, a thermometer in the cloudy yellow mixture. Label the cross, the flask, the observer and the stopwatch. |
| Nitrogen dioxide and dinitrogen tetroxide in a sealed syringe (pressure change) | 8464, 8462 | symbol `gasSyringe` | Three pictures of a gas syringe, or three gas syringes side by side. First: a brown gas (Brown gas preset) at the starting volume. Second: the plunger pushed in at once, the volume smaller and the brown colour darker. Third: the plunger held in, the same small volume, and the colour fading to a paler brown as the equilibrium shifts to the colourless N2O4. Labels: brown NO2, colourless N2O4, plunger pushed in. |
| Heating hydrated copper sulfate (a reversible reaction) | 8464, 8462 | template `reversibleHeating` | Use the reversibleHeating template: two boiling tubes, each in its own holder: the first slopes with its mouth down, blue crystals on its lower wall and the flame under them; the second holds white powder, with a dropper above it and drops falling. |
| Laboratory cracking of a hydrocarbon | 8464, 8462 | template `crackingApparatus` | Use the crackingApparatus template: a boiling tube nearly level, held by a clamp near its mouth whose arm runs to the stand behind the tube; a delivery tube runs along the floor of a trough into an inverted, water-filled, clamped test tube. The warning is plain text. |
| Fermentation of a sugar solution (apparatus) | 8462 | template `fermentationApparatus` | Use the fermentationApparatus template: a flask standing in a beaker of warm water with a thermometer at 35 degrees; the delivery tube from the bung, the only opening, dips into limewater in a test tube in a small beaker. |
| Testing the products of burning a hydrocarbon fuel | 8464, 8462 | template `combustionProducts` | Use the combustionProducts template: an inverted funnel clamped over a spirit burner; the funnel, a U-tube in ice, limewater and "to pump" are joined by glass and rubber tubing through bungs. |
| Bromine water test for an alkene | 8464, 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with two tubes in a rack: bromine water (Orange preset) with an alkane, which stays orange; and with an alkene, which goes colourless (Colourless solution preset). Labels say which is which. A dropper above the tubes. |
| Paper chromatogram with Rf measurements | 8464, 8462 | symbol `chromatographyPaper` | Use the chromatography paper symbol, developed: a pencil start line near the bottom, several spots (a pure substance gives one spot, a mixture several) and the solvent front line near the top. Add two dimension lines (a line with tick end caps) parallel to the edge: from the start line to the centre of one spot, and from the start line to the solvent front, each with its length in millimetres. Beside it, Rf = distance moved by the spot divided by the distance moved by the solvent. |
| Paper chromatography apparatus | 8464, 8462 | template `paperChromatography` | Use the paperChromatography template: a beaker with a little solvent, a paper hanging from a rod across the rim, the pencil start line above the solvent level, and the spots on the line. Add a watch glass or lid on the beaker when the question asks for the lid. Label beaker, solvent, pencil line, paper. |
| Filtration apparatus (separating an insoluble solid) | 8464, 8462 | template `filtration` | Use the filtration template: a funnel with fluted or folded filter paper standing in the neck of a conical flask, the residue (for example sand) on the paper and the filtrate in the flask. Label funnel, filter paper, residue, filtrate. |
| Tests for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and chlorine | 8464, 8462 | template `gasTests` | Use the gasTests template: one rack of five test tubes holds the four gas tests: hydrogen and oxygen with a splint (at the mouth, and in the tube), carbon dioxide (a source tube whose delivery tube runs into limewater) and chlorine. The result of each test is a plain-text caption. |
| Test for a carbonate (acid, then limewater) | 8462 | template `carbonateTest` | Use the carbonateTest template: a test tube of carbonate with a dropper of acid in one bung hole and a delivery tube from the other hole into limewater in a second test tube; both tubes stand in a rack. |
| Flame test apparatus (nichrome wire in a blue flame) | 8462 | template `flameTest` | Use the flameTest template: a Bunsen burner on a heatproof mat with a blue flame, and a nichrome wire loop held in the edge of the flame. Add a test tube of dilute acid beside it for cleaning the wire. Labels: nichrome wire, blue flame, sample, acid for cleaning. |
| Halide and sulfate precipitate tests in test tubes | 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with four tubes. Halides: add dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate; chloride gives a white precipitate, bromide a cream one, iodide a yellow one (the Cream and Yellow presets). Sulfate: add dilute hydrochloric acid then barium chloride; a white precipitate. Labels give the reagents and the colour. |
| Metal hydroxide precipitates with sodium hydroxide solution | 8462 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with six tubes: aluminium, calcium and magnesium ions give white precipitates (aluminium dissolving in excess alkali), copper(II) gives a blue precipitate, iron(II) a green one, iron(III) a brown one. Labels give the ion and the colour. A dropper above the tubes. |
| Water analysis and purification (distillation set-up) | 8464, 8462 | template `simpleDistillation` | Use the simpleDistillation template: a conical flask of salty water on a gauze over a Bunsen burner, a two-hole bung with a thermometer and a delivery tube to a test tube standing in a beaker of ice and water. For the dissolved-solids test add the crystallisation picture (an evaporating basin heated over a beaker). For the pH test a beaker with a pH probe or indicator paper. |
| Rusting experiment (nails in test tubes) | 8462 | template `rustingTubes` | Use the rustingTubes template: four test tubes in a rack, each with a nail (the nail symbol); rust is a thin orange-brown layer at the foot of tubes 1 and 4, tube 3 has a bung, and a plain note explains the rust. |
| Hazard symbols (the nine GHS pictograms) | 8464, 8462 | symbol `hazardSymbol` | Use the hazardSymbol symbol: a diamond with a black picture inside, one of the nine GHS pictograms chosen by `hazard` (explosive, flammable, oxidising, gasUnderPressure, corrosive, toxic, harmful, health, environment). With `name` on, the name of the hazard is written under the diamond. The border is a plain black outline (rule S6): the real red border is not drawn. |
| Heating a liquid in a beaker (Bunsen burner, tripod, gauze, thermometer) | 8464, 8462 | template `heatingBeaker` | Use the heatingBeaker template: a Bunsen burner on a heatproof mat under a tripod and gauze, a beaker of water (60 percent) on the gauze and a thermometer in the water. Labels: burner, gauze, tripod, beaker, thermometer. This is the safe heating of apparatus and technique 2, and it is also the water bath of the temperature practicals. |
| Fractional distillation in the laboratory (ethanol and water) | 8464, 8462 | template `fractionalDistillationLab` | Use the fractionalDistillationLab template: a heating mantle, a flask, a packed column, a still head with a thermometer (its bulb level with the side arm), a sloping Liebig condenser (water in at the low port) and a receiver adaptor in the neck of a collecting flask, so that the system is open at one point. |
| Formula triangle (moles, concentration and similar) | 8464, 8462 | symbol `formulaTriangle` | Use the formulaTriangle symbol: a triangle split by a horizontal and a vertical line into three parts, one quantity at the top and two at the bottom. The presets are moles (m over n and Mr), concentration (n over c and V), gasVolume (V over n and 24) and yield (actual over % and max); custom takes your own three texts (physics: V over I and R, or speed over distance and time). Set hide to top, left or right to leave one part empty, for a worksheet. |
| Collecting a gas by downward or upward delivery | 8464, 8462 | template `gasCollection` | Use the gasCollection template: downward delivery and upward delivery side by side, with a lid under the inverted jar; a plain-text note under each says which gases it suits. |
| Testing whether a substance conducts electricity | 8464, 8462 | template `conductivityTest` | Use the conductivityTest template: a cell and a lamp in series with two carbon rods that dip into the sample without touching each other. |

## Chemistry, KS5

| diagram | courses | use | how |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Redox titration with potassium manganate(VII) (iron(II) or ethanedioate) | 7405 | template `titration` | Use the titration template with the Purple preset in the burette: purple manganate(VII) solution in the burette, and in the conical flask on the white tile an acidified solution of iron(II) ions or ethanedioate ions. The end point is the first permanent pale pink in the flask, because manganate(VII) is its own indicator. Labels: burette, manganate(VII), flask, tile. |
| Making up a standard solution in a volumetric flask (practical 1) | 7405 | template `standardSolution` | Use the standardSolution template: a volumetric flask with a filter funnel in its neck, a wash bottle and a beaker beside it, the solution below the graduation mark, and a label on the neck. Add a second picture of the made-up solution with its stopper and the meniscus on the mark. |
| Measuring an enthalpy change by calorimetry (practical 2) | 7405 | template `spiritBurnerCalorimetry` | Use the spiritBurnerCalorimetry template for combustion: a metal can of water clamped above a spirit burner with a thermometer in the water. For a solution reaction use the temperatureChange template (polystyrene cup with lid and thermometer in a beaker). Labels: can, water, thermometer, spirit burner, draught shield (optional). |
| How the rate of a reaction changes with temperature (practical 3) | 7405 | template `disappearingCross` | Use the disappearingCross template (the flask stands on the cross paper, with a thermometer in the mixture) and add a separate beaker of warm water beside it for the temperature control: the template has no water bath. Label the flask, cross, observer and thermometer. |
| Test-tube tests for cations and anions (practical 4) | 7405 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with the tests in the list: Group 2 cations with sodium hydroxide and with sulfate, ammonium with sodium hydroxide and damp red litmus paper at the tube mouth, halide ions with silver nitrate then ammonia, hydroxide ions, carbonate with acid and limewater, and sulfate with barium chloride. Labels give the reagent and the result. |
| Distillation of a product from a reaction (practical 5) | 7405 | template `distillation` | Use the distillation template: a round-bottomed flask in a heating mantle, still head with a thermometer in an adaptor, a Liebig condenser sloping down with water in at the lower port, a receiver adaptor and a conical flask. Labels for each part and the water direction. |
| Tests for alcohols, aldehydes, alkenes and carboxylic acids (practical 6) | 7405 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template, with a beaker of warm water for the aldehyde tests. Tubes: acidified dichromate with an alcohol or aldehyde (orange to green), Tollens' reagent with an aldehyde (the contents model cannot draw a silver mirror; a grey powder layer at the foot of the tube, labelled as the mirror, is the nearest), Fehling's or Benedict's solution (brick-red precipitate, the Brick-red preset), bromine water with an alkene (orange to colourless), sodium carbonate with a carboxylic acid (bubbles). |
| Measuring rate by initial rate and by continuous monitoring (practical 7) | 7405 | template `rateGasSyringe` | Use the rateGasSyringe template for volume against time, the massLoss template for mass against time, or the disappearingCross template for a clock reaction. A colorimeter route uses the instrument box symbol. Labels as in the GCSE pictures. |
| Measuring the EMF of an electrochemical cell (practical 8) | 7405 | template `electrochemicalCell` | Use the electrochemicalCell template: two beakers with metal strips in their own solutions, a salt bridge (filter paper soaked in potassium nitrate) between them, and a high-resistance voltmeter joined to the two strips. Mark the positive and negative terminals and the cell notation. |
| pH change in a titration with a pH meter (practical 9) | 7405 | template `phCurve` | Use the phCurve template: a beaker on a hot plate with a stirrer bar, a pH probe in the solution wired to a pH meter, and a burette above. Labels for the probe, meter, burette and stirrer. |
| Heating under reflux (practical 10) | 7405 | template `reflux` | Use the reflux template: a round-bottomed flask with anti-bumping granules in a heating mantle, an upright Liebig condenser with water in at the lower port and out at the upper port, a clamp at the flask neck. A label says that the top of the condenser is open to the air and is the only opening. |
| Separating and drying an organic liquid (practical 10) | 7405 | template `separatingFunnelUse` | Use the separatingFunnelUse template: the funnel clamped upright with the stopper off, two layers labelled aqueous and organic, a beaker under the tap. For drying, a conical flask with the organic liquid and a spatula of anhydrous drying agent. |
| Filtration under reduced pressure and recrystallisation (practical 10) | 7405 | template `buchnerFiltration` | Use the buchnerFiltration template: a Buchner funnel with filter paper in a one-hole bung on a Buchner flask, the side arm joined by thick rubber tube to a pump (label: to pump), the solid on the paper and the filtrate in the flask. |
| Measuring a melting point to test purity (practical 10) | 7405 | template `meltingPoint` | Use the meltingPoint template: a melting point apparatus block with a thermometer and a capillary tube holding the solid, both in the holes of the heated block. Labels for thermometer, capillary tube and sample. |
| Test-tube reactions of transition metal ions in solution (practical 11) | 7405 | template `testTubeReactions` | Use the testTubeReactions template with tubes of aqueous ions and their products: copper(II) blue with a pale blue precipitate and a deep blue solution in excess ammonia, iron(II) pale green, iron(III) yellow-brown, chromium(III) green, and vanadium in its four oxidation states reduced with zinc (yellow, blue, green, violet). Labels give the ion and the colour. |
| Separating species by thin-layer chromatography (practical 12) | 7405 | template `tlc` | Use the tlc template: a beaker with a little solvent, a plate leaning in it with the pencil start line above the solvent, a watch glass as a lid, and the developed spots and solvent front. Add the Rf measurement lines as for the GCSE chromatogram. |
